faq.title: Everything you need to know
faq.subtitle: Got questions? We have answers. If you can't find what you're looking for, feel free to contact our team.

items.a:
VidyaSetu is an AI-powered learning platform built to make education accessible to every child—regardless of language, learning needs, or internet connectivity.

It combines adaptive learning, regional languages, offline-first education, assistive technology, life-skills learning, and AI-powered support for teachers and parents in one ecosystem.

items.q: 02 — What makes it different from a normal AI tutor?
items.a:
We don't just make AI explain a lesson—we make the learning experience adapt to the learner.

Unlike a conventional AI tutor, VidyaSetu combines personalized learning + accessibility + regional languages + offline learning + assistive technology + teacher/parent collaboration.

A child doesn't simply receive an answer. The platform learns from their progress and adapts what they learn, how they learn it, and how much support they receive.

items.q: 03 — How does AI personalize learning for my child?
items.a:
Every child learns differently.

Our platform can use assessment results, learning progress, interactions, pace, and performance to build an individual learning profile. The system can then adapt the difficulty, pace, explanation style, content format, and activities to better match the child's needs.

Instead of asking every child to fit the curriculum, we make the curriculum fit the child.

items.q: 04 — Can it work without the internet?
items.a:
Yes—that's one of our core principles.

The platform follows an offline-first approach, allowing essential learning experiences to continue even when internet connectivity is unavailable. Learning activity can be stored locally and synchronized when connectivity returns.

This makes the platform especially relevant for low-connectivity schools and communities where continuous internet access cannot be assumed.

items.q: 05 — How does it support children with different learning needs?
items.a:
Accessibility is built into the learning experience—not added as an afterthought.

Depending on the learner's needs, the platform can provide features such as dyslexia-friendly reading modes, adjustable text and spacing, reduced cognitive load, high-contrast interfaces, captions, visual learning, sign-language support, and AAC-style communication.

The goal isn't to create a separate classroom for every child. It's to create one learning environment that can adapt to different children.

Snap & Learn turns an ordinary textbook page into an interactive AI lesson.

A child photographs a page, and AI can read the content, understand it, simplify the explanation, translate it into a preferred language, narrate it, and generate interactive questions.

So instead of needing a specially digitized textbook, a printed page can become an accessible, personalized learning experience.

items.q: 07 — How do teachers and parents become part of the learning journey?
items.a:
Learning shouldn't stop at the student's screen.

Our Teacher/Parent AI Co-Pilot turns learning progress into useful, human-friendly insights.

Teachers can receive actionable recommendations about where a child may need additional support, while parents can receive simple updates—potentially through voice in their preferred language—so they understand what the child is learning and how they can help.

AI connects the child, teacher, and parent instead of isolating learning to an app.

No. It makes teachers more powerful.

AI can handle repetitive tasks such as identifying learning patterns, adapting content, and summarizing progress. Teachers remain responsible for the human side of education—understanding the child, building confidence, mentoring, encouraging, and making important decisions.

AI personalizes the learning. Humans personalize the care.

science.text: Which part of the plant is primarily responsible for photosynthesis?
science.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll — the green pigment that absorbs sunlight to power photosynthesis.

science.text: What gas do plants release as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
science.explanation: Oxygen (O₂) is released when plants split water molecules using sunlight energy.

science.text: What process converts liquid water into water vapor in the water cycle?
science.explanation: Evaporation is when liquid water gains heat energy to become water vapor.

science.text: In which part of the chloroplast does the light-dependent reaction occur?
science.explanation: Light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes where chlorophyll resides.

math.text: 3/5 of a class of 40 students are girls. How many boys are there?
What is the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm?
math.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm²

history.text: Who led the Salt March of 1930?
history.explanation: Gandhi led the 241-mile Dandi March to protest the British salt tax.

history.text: Which ruler converted to Buddhism after the Kalinga War?
history.explanation: Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism's path of non-violence after Kalinga.

geo.text: Which is the longest river in India?
geo.explanation: The Ganga stretches ~2,525 km, making it the longest river in India.

geo.text: What climate type does the Thar Desert have?
geo.explanation: The Thar Desert has an arid climate with very hot temperatures and minimal rainfall.
